SUAS-017 — SuperUnicode East Asian Script Data

The runtime counterpart of UAX #60: one 12-byte script record, a compact classification range table, a parallel UAX #60 metadata table, and a total O(1) answer for every East Asian codepoint.

SUAS-017 (SUEASD) is the seventeenth SuperUnicode Architecture Standard and the runtime counterpart of UAX #60, "Data for East Asian Scripts". Four text manifests publish the ancillary data for Jurchen, Nushu, Small Seal and Tangut; Scripts.txt carries the primary script assignment. SUEASD compiles both layers into a byte-packed table with a bounded lookup, so an input method, font engine or terminal can classify a codepoint without parsing a manifest.

SUEASD does not re-implement SUAS-009 (SIP). SIP carries the Han radical-stroke and ideographic attributes; SUEASD routes the East Asian scripts and carries the UAX #60 ancillary data for the scripts outside the Han core. The two compose; neither re-derives the other.

Why a binary property

Aspect UAX #60 / text manifests SUEASD
Script Scripts.txt scanned per query A 12-byte static record read from a fixed range table
Ancillary data Four source files parsed and joined per query One curated record plus a parallel metadata row
Radical-stroke A "12.4" text field A uint16_t radical and a uint8_t stroke count
Readings and sources Free-form text values FNV-1a hashes of the primary fields
Numeric value Parsed from text A uint16_t integer
Modern CJK A string join A uint32_t codepoint equivalence
Unlisted codepoint Undefined A total algorithmic default — every East Asian codepoint answers
Failure mode An implementer’s own reconciliation The verifier names the first of fourteen defects

The script record

Five fields, 12 bytes, no padding on any supported ABI. They are the seeding sketch’s fields, verbatim: codepoint, script_mask, primary_script, source_region and reserved.

typedef struct {
uint32_t codepoint; /* 31-bit SUCS codepoint */
uint32_t script_mask; /* Packed script property flags */
uint16_t primary_script; /* SUEASD_SCRIPT_* identifier */
uint8_t source_region; /* SUEASD_REGION_* class */
uint8_t reserved; /* must be zero */
} sueasd_script_entry_t;

The record carries no source mask, radical-stroke counts, numeric value, raw-field hashes or modern-CJK equivalence: those live in a parallel 24-byte metadata table aligned one-to-one with the curated table. The radical is 16 bits because the Small Seal and Tangut radical sets are numbered past 255.

Classification ranges

Enumerating every East Asian codepoint would exceed the 65,534 index-slot ceiling, so SUEASD resolves a base record from 78 disjoint, coalesced ranges derived from Scripts.txt and consults the curated table only for the UAX #60 ancillary layer. A range is 12 bytes: first, last, primary_script and base_flags.

Script Repertoire Ancillary
Han U+2E80–33479, U+2F800–2FA1D Classification ranges only (SIP carries the Han details)
Hangul U+1100–11FF, U+AC00–D7A3, compatibility Jamo Classification ranges only
Hiragana / Katakana U+3041–309F, U+30A1–30FF, supplementary kana Classification ranges only
Bopomofo U+02EA–02EB, U+3105–312F, U+31A0–31BF Classification ranges only
Jurchen U+18E00–191D2 914 curated codepoints
Nushu U+16FE1, U+1B170–1B2FB 396 curated codepoints
Small Seal U+3D000–3FC3F 11,328 curated codepoints
Tangut U+16FE0, U+17000–18DF2 6,177 curated codepoints
Khitan Small Script U+16FE4, U+18B00–18CFF Classification only — UAX #60 has no source data yet

Flags and roles

The sketch’s four flags are preserved, including the two macros it printed without an =. SUEASD adds the orthogonal roles it derives from position in the repertoire: HAN_CORE / HAN_RADICAL / HAN_COMPAT, KANA, JAMO / SYLLABLE, and the UAX #60 presence flags SOURCE_DATA / READING / RS / NUMERIC / MODERN_CJK. IDEOGRAPHIC marks the modern CJK grid role (Han, Bopomofo, Small Seal); the covered scripts are identified by their script id and source mask.

UAX #60 field SUEASD representation
kJURC_Src / kNSHU_DubenSrc / kTGT_MergedSrc source_mask bit plus source_hash of the primary value
kJURC_NCReading / kNSHU_Reading source_mask bit plus reading_hash
kJURC_RSUnicode / kTGT_RSUnicode / kSEAL_Rad radical, stroke_count and aux_hash
kJURC_Numeric / kTGT_Numeric numeric_value
kSEAL_MCJK modern_cjk codepoint equivalence
Distinct rows source_count

Totality and neography

A codepoint inside an East Asian range or the Native & Neography Plane carve-out (0x00160000–0x0016FFFF) always resolves. If no range and no curated row exist, SUEASD synthesizes the default of section 6 — UNKNOWN script, NONE region, and the CUSTOM_SCRIPT flag in RNUR — while suas_sueasd_is_east_asian and suas_sueasd_is_curated remain false. A renderer can therefore answer for a newly declared RNUR coordinate or a non-East-Asian codepoint without special-casing a missing lookup.

The shipped table carries 18,815 curated records drawn from the four UAX #60 manifests, and 78 classification ranges that make the property total over the East Asian repertoire.

Verification names the defect

suas_sueasd_validate_table returns the first of fourteen named outcomes: a NULL table, a count over capacity, an unordered pair, a duplicate codepoint, a codepoint past the space, an inadmissible codepoint, a bad script or region, a non-zero reserved byte, an ideographic or kana disagreement, jamo and syllable together, or a malformed range table. An empty registry is valid: an implementation with no curated records ships zero rows and conforms.

Classification note

SUEASD is a SUAS core invariant, registered as SUAS-017, the number immediately after SUAS-016 (SUKEMET). One element of the SUTS framing survives deliberately: the table contents are version data, so an implementation with no curated records ships an empty table and remains conformant — while the engine, the record layout, the taxonomy and the verification rules are mandatory architecture.

Reference implementation: include/suas/suas_sueasd.h + src/suas/suas_sueasd.c (freestanding C99, no heap), registered in suas_static and in the SSRE registry as a MANDATORY specification.

Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-017-sueasd.md in the repository.
